name: Driftwood Cove
hours: Always open; a ten-minute scramble west of the Commons over the headland. Lifeguarded only on organised beach days.
sight: A crescent of pale sand between two black lava headlands, with water that goes from glass-green to deep blue in thirty strokes. Bleached driftwood trunks lie like benches; a rope swing hangs from a leaning palm. No building is in sight. By night the sand is cold and silver, and the surf lights up green wherever you step in it.
things: Swim, properly, in the open sea
Join a beach day: volleyball, a cool box, cards weighted down with shells
Snorkel over the reef shelf and see parrotfish and one grumpy moray
Build something ambitious out of driftwood
Walk the tideline for sea-glass and shells
At night: wade in and watch the water glow round your ankles
secret: The island at its most innocent: beach days Days 7, 147, 203. Swimsuit scenes are light and tasteful; Georgie, if present, has armbands of dignity and a sun hat. Night swims here are key scenes for Sunny and Saoirse. The glow is ordinary plankton — until D27, after which on some nights it gathers into slow square patterns before breaking up. Among the sea-glass after D27: beads of black fused glass, carried round by the current from the north.
